title: Tabs as Steps
approval: Design approved: friction plan part 3, tabs as steps

short.lead: You described the flow you want: Capture a stray thought from anywhere, Sort it, Organize with Tidy up and Triage, plan on the Roadmap, then Focus and Review. This plan follows it exactly. Capture is not a tab. The jot box sits at the top of every tab. The five tabs are Sort, Organize, Roadmap, Focus and Review. The Roadmap replaces the Projects screen and the Board. Each project has sections. Each section holds milestones. Each milestone has its own Up next, In progress, Review and Done columns. You choose how much each milestone counts and how its progress is measured. All the numbers in the pictures are made-up examples.
short.hint: Tap each row to see its picture. Start with 'Your flow, as five tabs', then the table at the end, which shows where every feature of Projects and Board goes.
items: The dashed band at the top is Capture: the jot box shown on every tab, and the J key opens it from anywhere on desktop. Below it are the five tabs in your order, each with the question it answers. The grey boxes under each tab name today's screens that move into it.
Read the five tabs left to right and check that the order matches your flow.

items.alt: Capture band with a jot box above five numbered tab cards: Sort, Organize, Roadmap, Focus and Review, each listing today's screens that move into it
items.caption: The flow and where today's screens go. A drawing, not built.

items: The jot box is at the top, as on every tab. Below it, one thought at a time gets a project, a priority (required) and a due date (optional), as in part 2. The tabs at the bottom are numbered 1 to 5. Sort and Review each show a count of items waiting for you.
Check that the jot box at the top doesn't crowd the sorting.

items.alt: Phone drawing: jot box, the Sort tab with one thought, project chips, priority and due buttons, File to Chores and Later, and five numbered tabs
items.caption: Sort on a phone. A drawing, not built.

items: With the switch on Area (here Apps), each row is a project. Each block is the milestone that project is working on in one section, with its own measure, such as screens tested or beta testers. The percent under each project name adds up its milestones, giving more weight to the ones you said count more.
Check that one block per section is enough to see where each project stands.

items.alt: Desktop drawing: Roadmap for the Apps area, three project rows, each with milestone blocks tagged by section and their own measures
items.caption: Roadmap for a group of projects. A drawing, not built.

items: With the switch on Project, the page shows the project's sections in order. Each milestone opens into four columns: Up next, In progress, Review and Done. You can drag a task to any column, in any direction. You can also drag a milestone to another section; the dashed gap shows where it will land. The buttons '+ Add a task', '+ Add a milestone' and '+ Add a section' sit where they apply. The bar at the top splits the project's progress by milestone, so you can see how much each milestone added.
Follow the task 'Test on phone' as it is dragged in the picture, then tell me whether dragging looks right to you.

items.alt: Desktop drawing: Focus Deck at 26 percent, a split progress bar, section 1 Foundations with milestone Start here screen open into four columns and a task being dragged, a closed Areas milestone, and section 2 with a dashed drop gap
items.caption: One project's roadmap. A drawing, not built.

items: Tapping a milestone's name opens its settings. The slider sets how much it counts toward the project. 'Measure progress by' offers four ways: Tasks done (how many tasks are finished), Task size (small counts 1, medium 2, large 3), Your own number (you give it a name and a target), or A checklist (you list what 'done' means).
Check that the four measures cover how you'd judge a milestone.

items.alt: Phone drawing: milestone settings sheet with a slider at 40 percent and four measure options, Your own number selected as screens tested on a phone 2 of 4
items.caption: Milestone settings on a phone. A drawing, not built.

items: Start here on top, then choose

Start here's three picks and 'Pick one for me' sit at the top, beside 'Doing now', which lists what is in progress. 'Or choose it yourself' below is the carousel from part 2. The All / Area / Project switch works here too.
Check that Start here belongs on Focus rather than a tab of its own.

items.alt: Desktop drawing: Start here with three picks and Pick one for me, a Doing now column with two tasks, and a carousel of Home projects below
items.caption: Focus on desktop. A drawing, not built.

items: 'Waiting for your review' lists tasks in the Review column, each with 'Looks good · Done' or 'Needs more work'. 'Needs more work' moves the task back to In progress. 'Done this week' lists what you finished, with Undo.
Read the two buttons, 'Looks good · Done' and 'Needs more work', and tell me if either is unclear.

items.alt: Phone drawing: Review tab with two waiting tasks and their buttons, and Done this week with Undo
items.caption: Review on a phone. A drawing, not built.

items: Nothing from Projects or Board is lost
Each row is something a screen does today and where it goes. 'Same' means it works as today, 'Moved' means it's reached a different way, and 'Merged' means two copies become one.
Look for anything you use that isn't in the table.

changes: Five tabs: Sort, Organize, Roadmap, Focus, Review
Numbered in your order, on phone and desktop.
The All / Area / Project switch sits at the top of each.
Becomes the jot box at the top of every tab; J opens it on desktop.
Becomes the Roadmap, on All, Area or one Project.
Adding, editing, the GitHub link and Sync all come with it.
Its columns live inside each milestone, plus a Review column.
Drag in any direction, as today.
Drag sections and milestones; set what each milestone counts and how it's measured.
Project progress is weighted by milestone.
Moves to the top of Focus.
Three picks and Pick one for me stay.
Waiting for review, and what you finished.
'Needs more work' sends a task back to In progress.
Task details, your data and sync
choices: review
Should Review become a real fourth column for every task?
Yes, a fourth column
Tasks go Up next, In progress, Review, Done. On GitHub it sets and reads your Needs review label.
No, keep it as a GitHub label
Only GitHub issues can wait for review; tasks you add in the app can't.
I suggest Yes, because your flow moves tasks between review and in progress in both directions.
weights
How should a new milestone's weight start?
Equal shares
Each milestone starts with an equal share and you change any you like.
By task count
Milestones with more tasks start with a bigger share. This is the plain task percent, which you said doesn't tell the whole story.
I suggest equal shares, because then the percent only changes when you choose to give a milestone a bigger share.
starthere
Where should Start here live?
Top of Focus
Five tabs, matching your flow, with the picks above Doing now.
Its own tab before Focus
Six tabs, one of which isn't in the flow you described.
I suggest the top of Focus, because your flow goes straight from Roadmap to Focus.
board
Should the old Board stay as an optional layout?
No, remove it
Its columns live inside each milestone, so nothing is shown twice.
Yes, as a Settings option
The same tasks would appear in two places.
I suggest removing it, because you asked for no views that repeat each other.

wrapup.summary: The tabs follow your flow: the jot box on every tab for Capture, then Sort, Organize, Roadmap, Focus and Review. The Roadmap holds sections, milestones and four columns per milestone, and you decide how much each milestone counts.
wrapup.changing: Changed: the tabs, the Jotter, Projects, Board and Start here. Added: sections, milestone settings, weighted progress and the Review tab. Kept: task details, your data and sync.
wrapup.blocking: Waiting on your answers to the four questions in the Choices section of this page, and to the open questions on the part 2 page. Nothing is built until you approve.
wrapup.next: After you answer, I will fold parts 1, 2 and 3 into one build order and open GitHub issues for each part.
